core1b.fresh_task: Three labelled markers are A=(1,1), B=(4,1), C=(2,3). An image report gives A′=(−1,−1), B′=(−4,−1), C′=(−2,−3), and claims one mirror created it. A second report gives A″=(−1,1), B″=(−4,1), C″=(−2,3). Justify which report can be a single reflection and identify the simplest transformation for the other. Use signed orientation as evidence.
core1b.protected_work: Use an oriented non-collinear configuration to distinguish a single reflection from a rotation or even number of reflections, rather than rely on verbal left/right labels.

stages.predict: Before solving, predict the outcome or relationship and record uncertainty.
stages.attempt: Three labelled markers are A=(1,1), B=(4,1), C=(2,3). An image report gives A′=(−1,−1), B′=(−4,−1), C′=(−2,−3), and claims one mirror created it. A second report gives A″=(−1,1), B″=(−4,1), C″=(−2,3). Justify which report can be a single reflection and identify the simplest transformation for the other. Use signed orientation as evidence.
stages.reconstruct: Original signed double area det(B−A,C−A)=6. First report vectors (−3,0),(−1,−2) give +6: orientation preserved, impossible for one reflection of non-collinear labelled points; it is a 180° rotation about origin (or two perpendicular reflections). Second gives det((−3,0),(−1,2))=−6, and all points satisfy x→−x, y unchanged, so reflection across x=0.
stages.diagnose: Only if your saved response exhibits this error: Equating any apparent left/right change with a single mirror reflection. Otherwise record insufficient evidence.
stages.repair: Track two independent displacement vectors and compute their determinant before naming the transformation.
stages.boundary_test: Why does a collinear triple of markers fail to distinguish the handedness of a general planar isometry?

core1b.fresh_task: An oriented triangle A=(0,0), B=(2,0), C=(0,1) is observed as A′=(0,0), B′=(0,2), C′=(1,0). A second observation has A″=(0,0), B″=(0,2), C″=(−1,0). Distinguish reflection versus rotation using signed orientation and identify each mapping.

stages.attempt: An oriented triangle A=(0,0), B=(2,0), C=(0,1) is observed as A′=(0,0), B′=(0,2), C′=(1,0). A second observation has A″=(0,0), B″=(0,2), C″=(−1,0). Distinguish reflection versus rotation using signed orientation and identify each mapping.
stages.reconstruct: Original determinant +2. First +x→+y, +y→+x gives determinant −2: reflection across y=x. Second +x→+y, +y→−x gives determinant +2: rotation +90°. A single reflection cannot realize second labelled triangle.
